entities.name: ATP synthase gamma chain
observations: Query sequence is 281 aa and exactly matches reviewed UniProt reference Q6F203 from Mesoplasma florum.
Predicted molecular weight is 31.4 kDa; theoretical pI is 5.50.
The sequence contains an ATP-synt domain (PF00231.25) spanning residues 3–279.
The gamma chain is a peripheral component of the F-type proton-transporting ATP synthase complex.
It contributes to rotational ATP synthase regulation and coupling between proton movement and ATP synthesis; it is not the catalytic alpha/beta ATP-binding subunit.

entities.name: F-type ATP synthase complex
observations: The gamma chain is part of the membrane-associated F-type ATP synthase, whose membrane sector conducts protons and whose soluble F1 sector synthesizes ATP.
The complex supports proton-motive-force-driven ATP synthesis.

entities.name: Bacterial plasma membrane
observations: The gamma chain is annotated as a peripheral membrane protein associated with the plasma membrane through the ATP synthase complex.
The protein has no predicted transmembrane segment in the provided sequence; membrane association is therefore through complex assembly rather than an intrinsic membrane helix.
